docs.title: callcat.ai Documentation
docs.text:
callcat.ai is a platform for businesses to deploy AI voice agents that answer inbound phone calls, take web calls from a button on their website, and hand off to a human when needed. You configure an agent's persona, voice, knowledge, and the questions it should ask, then review every call's recording, transcript, and post-call summary from one dashboard.

This site is the reference and how-to documentation for operating that platform.

  • New here?

    Start with Core concepts to learn the vocabulary — operators, clients, agents, calls, and embeds.

  • Building agents

    Jump to Agents to configure a persona, design the conversation, and set up call forwarding.

  • Looking for something?

    Use the search box (top right) — every page is indexed. Or browse by Tags.

  • In-product help

    The ? help buttons inside the dashboard link straight to the relevant article and section here.

docs.title: Accounts, sign-in & onboarding
docs.text: Your login belongs to an operator — your business workspace. Everything you create (clients, agents, calls) lives inside it, and your teammates share it.

docs.title: Signing in
docs.text:
callcat.ai supports two sign-in methods, and both lead to the same dashboard:

  • Email & password — register with an email and password, then log in.
  • Single sign-on — sign in with your connected identity provider; your session is exchanged for dashboard access automatically.

Use whichever your organization prefers. If you were invited to an existing operator, follow the invite link and sign in — you'll join that workspace rather than creating a new one.

Forgotten which one you used?

If email/password doesn't work, you may have signed up via SSO (or vice-versa). Try the other method, or ask a teammate to re-send an invite.

docs.title: First-run onboarding
docs.text:
The first time a new operator signs in, a short onboarding flow captures the essentials — your business name and basic preferences — so your agents and emails can identify your business correctly. You can change any of it later in Settings.

After onboarding, the natural next steps are in Getting started: add a client, build an agent, and place a test call.

docs.title: Inviting your team
docs.text: Bring colleagues into your operator from Settings → Team. Each teammate gets a role that controls what they can do. Invited users join your operator and see the same clients and agents.

docs.title: Administration & roles
docs.text: callcat.ai has three roles. Most people are users; admin and super_admin unlock progressively more.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Role Can do user Day-to-day work — manage clients, agents, and review calls. admin Everything a user can, plus operator-level administration of your workspace. super_admin Platform-wide administration across operators (see below).

Assign roles when you invite teammates.

docs.title: Super-admin capabilities
docs.text:
Super-admins administer the platform itself, not just one workspace:

  • Approve new operators. When a business signs up, a super-admin reviews and activates the operator — and sets its billing currency at that point (see Billing → Multi-currency).
  • Tune plan pricing. Super-admins maintain a per-operator plan catalog — adding, renaming, reordering, and retuning the plans (base fee, included minutes, per-minute, overage, and forwarding rates) an operator's clients can be put on. This is the editable layer on top of the default plan templates.
  • Impersonate an operator. To support or troubleshoot, a super-admin can view a specific operator's workspace as if inside it, scoped to that operator's data.
  • Free-week packages. From the operator row's menu, set how many free weeks an operator may give its clients (default 5) and the cap per week (platform default 10 in the operator's currency), see the weeks already given, and void one early.

Currency is set at approval

An operator's billing currency is chosen when it's approved, before any billing exists. Everything defaults to GBP. See Billing.

docs.title: Operator feature switches
docs.text: Four features are off for every new operator. A super-admin turns each one on per operator, in the Super Admin dashboard (one switch per operator in the table). Regular users and admins cannot change them. Turning a switch off later hides the feature again but does not delete anything already built.

docs.title: Hebrew
docs.text: Lets the operator pick Hebrew agent personas and use the dashboard in Hebrew. Hebrew agents that already exist keep working whether the switch is on or off. The same switch is on the operator's own Settings page, visible to super-admins only.

docs.title: Order taking
docs.text: Shows the Catalog / product info and Order taking cards in the agent page for that operator. See Catalog & order taking. Without this switch an operator cannot add a menu or let an agent take orders.

docs.title: Decision tree
docs.text: Adds the Decision tree mode to the conversation design switcher for every agent of that operator. Use it for fully scripted calls.

docs.title: Bookings
docs.text: Shows the Bookings tab on every client of that operator, where an admin connects Cliniko and lets agents move and cancel appointments by phone. See Appointment bookings. While the switch is off, operator admins don't see the tab at all (super-admins still do, with a banner, but can't connect or save settings). The switch is checked on every booking request, so turning it off stops bookings for that operator's agents straight away, even mid-call. Nothing is deleted: turn it back on and the connection and settings are as they were.

docs.title: Restricted features
docs.text:
A few capabilities are limited to super-admins:

  • The Decision tree conversation design mode.
  • Certain restricted personas / voices (for example native Hebrew voices) in the voice picker.

Regular users won't see these options; that's expected.

docs.title: How callcat.ai works
docs.text: A high-level look at the moving parts, for developers and the technically curious. This describes the shape of the system — not its internal configuration.

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
callcat.ai is a set of focused services rather than one monolith:

Service Role Dashboard The web app you use to manage clients, agents, embeds, and review calls. Management API The backend that owns all data and serves the dashboard. Voice runtime The real-time voice pipeline that bridges callers and the AI provider, and produces transcripts and recordings. Embed gateway & SDK Mints short-lived tokens for web calls and provides the drop-in browser button. Billing Subscriptions, plans, usage metering, and invoices.

The dashboard talks only to the Management API; the voice runtime publishes what happens on a call as a stream of events that the API persists.

docs.title: How a call flows
docs.text:
Caller (phone, web, or test)
   │
   ▼
Voice runtime  ──►  AI provider (speech + language)
   │  publishes events: started, transcript, ended, transferred, analyzed
   ▼
Management API  ──►  stores the call, transcript, recording, summary
   │
   ▼
Dashboard  ──►  you review it
  1. A call arrives — from a phone number, a web embed button, or a browser test call.
  2. The voice runtime looks up the agent, builds its instructions from the persona, knowledge, questions, and conversation design, and starts talking.
  3. As the conversation happens, it streams events — the call started, each transcript turn, a transfer, the call ended, and a post-call analysis.
  4. The Management API records those into the call's history.
  5. You see the result in Calls.

docs.title: Channels
docs.text:
The same agent and the same pipeline serve three channels:

  • Phone — calls over the telephone network to an assigned phone number.
  • Web — browser calls from an embed, authorized by a short-lived token from the embed gateway.
  • Test — browser calls from the dashboard, for building and tuning agents.

docs.title: Integrating
docs.text:
The most common integration point is the web embed — a single script tag and a button put a live agent on any website. See Web calls & embeds.

This is the public overview

Operational details — deployment, secrets, and internal runbooks — live in callcat.ai's private engineering docs, not here.

docs.title: Billing
docs.text: callcat.ai bills per minute against a subscription plan on each client. This page is the operator-facing view of how charges are made up.

docs.title: Plans
docs.text:
Each client is on a plan that defines:

  • a monthly base fee,
  • an amount of included minutes,
  • a per-minute rate for usage,
  • an overage rate for minutes beyond the included bundle,
  • a forwarding rate for transferred minutes, and
  • limits on agents and phone numbers.

Operators have a plan catalog they can tune per their own needs, and pricing is multi-currency (the client's currency is set when the client is approved).

Test clients aren't billed

Clients in testing status, and test calls, are excluded from charges. Move a client to active when you're ready to bill it.

docs.title: How a charge is built
docs.text:
For a full month a client's charge is:

base fee
+ included-minutes bundle
+ overage      (extra minutes × overage rate)
+ forwarding   (transferred minutes × forwarding rate)

Partial months and mid-cycle plan changes are prorated:

  • Upgrades take effect immediately and are prorated.
  • Downgrades take effect at the start of the next month.

docs.title: The Billing area
docs.text:
The Billing tab shows, per period:

  • a summary strip — base, usage, overage, and forwarding totals,
  • a per-client breakdown you can search and export, and
  • billing history you can drill into month by month.

All amounts are shown in each client's currency.

docs.title: Free weeks
docs.text:
Each operator has a small number of free-week packages (5 by default; a super-admin can change this per operator). From a client's Info tab you can give an active client one free week:

  • it starts the moment you give it and ends exactly 7 days later, used or not;
  • calls placed in that window are not charged, until the waived usage reaches the cap (10 in your billing currency by default, e.g. £10 / $10; a super-admin can set a different cap for your operator). The call that crosses the cap is split, and later calls bill normally;
  • a client can only ever receive one free week, and it can't be taken back;
  • only a super-admin can extend a free week (by 7 days at a time, from its current end, or from now if it has already ended) or void it early. A week whose cap is already reached can't be extended.

A super-admin sets the allowance and the cap from the operator's Free weeks settings. The Use the default cap box keeps the platform cap (10 in the operator's currency). Untick it to type a different cap for that operator only.

When a free week reaches 90% of its cap, the operator's contact email and the platform team get one warning email, and the client shows an amber "almost used up" note on its Info tab and in the clients list.

Waived minutes never count against the plan's included bundle or overage. They show on the Billing tab and as an informational line on the invoice. Because calls are metered once a day, the "waived so far" figure lags by up to a day.

docs.title: Usage & reconciliation
docs.text: Completed calls are metered into the current billing cycle automatically. The figures you see reflect real usage at the client's effective pricing, so you can track charges without having to generate invoices first.

docs.title: Calls
docs.text: Every conversation an agent has — by phone, web, or test — is recorded as a call. The Calls area is where you review what happened.

docs.title: Call types
docs.text: Type Where it came from Phone A real inbound call to a phone number. Web A visitor using an embed button on a website. Test A browser test call from the dashboard (not billed).

docs.title: The calls list
docs.text: The list shows recent calls with the agent, caller, time, duration, and outcome. Filter by client, agent, date range, or type to find what you need. Open any call for its full detail.

docs.title: A call's detail
docs.text:
Each call captures:

  • Transcript — the full back-and-forth, turn by turn, with timestamps. On a live call the transcript streams in as it happens.
  • Recording — audio of the conversation you can play back.
  • Duration & cost — how long it ran and what it cost against the client's plan.
  • Outcome — whether it completed normally, was transferred to a human, or ended early.

docs.title: Transcript text direction
docs.text: For agents in a right-to-left language (such as Hebrew) the transcript opens right-to-left. A small switch above the transcript flips it to left-to-right, for example when a call is mostly English. It only changes how this window shows the text; the call and its stored transcript are not changed.

docs.title: Post-call analysis
docs.text:
Shortly after a call ends, callcat.ai adds an automatic analysis:

  • Summary — a short, readable recap of the conversation.
  • Sentiment — overall caller sentiment (positive, neutral, or negative).
  • Extracted data — the structured answers to your intake questions, pulled from what the caller said, plus anything captured by conditional instructions.

Summaries by email

Operators can have a summary emailed after each completed call — see Settings.

docs.title: Following up
docs.text: Use the summary and extracted data to follow up with callers — the agent's job is to capture the right information and route or escalate it, so a human can act on it quickly. For escalations during the call, see Call forwarding & transfers.

docs.title: Clients
docs.text: A client is an end-customer of your operator — the business whose calls your agents answer. Each client has its own agents, phone numbers, calls, branding, and subscription.

docs.title: Creating a client
docs.text:
From Clients → New client, set:

  • Name and industry — the industry can seed sensible defaults for new agents.
  • Contact details — name, email, phone.
  • Branding — a logo and colour used where the client is shown.

Once created, open the client to find tabs for Calls, Agents, Phone numbers, Embeds, and Info.

docs.title: Industry templates
docs.text:
The industry you choose isn't just a label — it drives industry templates. When you create a new agent for the client, the template for that industry seeds sensible starting points: a fitting greeting, a relevant set of intake questions, and a head start on the knowledge base.

Templates are only a starting point — every field stays fully editable, so you can tailor the agent from a sensible default instead of a blank page. Changing the client's industry affects the defaults offered to new agents, not ones you've already built.

docs.title: Client status
docs.text:
A client moves through a small set of states:

Status Meaning testing Set up but not yet billed — ideal while you build and test agents. active Live and billed against its plan. pending_deactivation Scheduled to deactivate (e.g. at the end of the billing period). inactive No longer served; data is retained but agents don't take calls.

Clients are deactivated, not deleted

There's no hard delete. Stopping service sets the client to inactive and preserves its history. A client with agents still attached can't be deactivated until those are handled.

docs.title: Plans & limits
docs.text: Each client carries a subscription plan that sets how many agents and phone numbers it can have, plus its per-minute pricing. When a client hits a limit, the relevant New action is disabled with a notice — upgrade the client's plan to raise it.

docs.title: Free week
docs.text: An active client can be given one free week from its Info tab: 7 days of calls at no charge, up to a cap. See Billing → Free weeks.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text: Everything in callcat.ai hangs off a small set of objects. Learn these once and the rest of the product makes sense.

docs.title: The hierarchy
docs.text:
Operator (your business)
└── Client (an end-customer you serve)
    └── Agent (an AI persona for that client)
        ├── Phone number (a Twilio number routed to the agent)
        ├── Embed (a web-call button on a website)
        └── Call (one phone or web conversation)

docs.title: Operator
docs.text: A business account / workspace. It owns your clients, agents, calls, and billing. The people who log in are users that belong to the operator. Roles are user, admin, and super_admin.

docs.title: Client
docs.text: An end-customer of yours — the business whose calls an agent answers. One operator has many clients. A client carries its own subscription plan, branding, and contact details. Clients are deactivated (not hard-deleted) when you stop serving them.

docs.title: Agent
docs.text:
A configured AI persona that belongs to a client. An agent has:

  • a persona and voice (see Configuring an agent),
  • a knowledge base and a list of intake questions,
  • a conversation design mode, and
  • call-forwarding rules for handing off to a human.

docs.title: Call
docs.text:
One voice conversation. A call has a type:

callType Origin phone A real inbound PSTN call to a Twilio number. web A web call from an embedded button on a website. test A browser test call placed from the dashboard.

Every call captures a transcript, a recording, duration, cost, and an optional post-call analysis (summary, sentiment, extracted data).

docs.title: Phone number
docs.text: A telephone number bound to an agent so inbound PSTN calls reach it. How many numbers you can attach depends on the client's plan.

docs.title: Embed
docs.text: A web-call configuration — the "Talk to us" button you drop onto a website. An embed routes web callers to a specific agent. Each embed has an allowlist of origins and its own concurrency limits.

docs.title: Embedding on your website
docs.text: A developer reference for putting a callcat.ai web-call button on a site. Create the embed in the dashboard first to get its id (emb_…) and add your site to its allowed origins.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Add the script once, then place a button anywhere. Pin a specific version and use the integrity hash shown when you create the embed:

<script
  src="https://cdn.vocadesk.com/embed/vX.Y.Z/vocadesk.min.js"
  integrity="sha384-…"
  crossorigin="anonymous"
  defer
></script>

<button data-vocadesk-embed="emb_abc123">Talk to us</button>

The script auto-binds any element with data-vocadesk-embed and handles microphone permission, the call UI, and connecting to the agent. It works regardless of where in the page it loads.

Pin a version

Always reference a specific vX.Y.Z and its integrity hash. There is no auto-updating "latest" URL — pinning is what keeps the integrity check valid.

docs.title: Mount programmatically
docs.text:
If you'd rather control placement in code:

const handle = window.Vocadesk.mount("#support-button", {
  embedId: "emb_abc123",
  label: "Talk to us",
});
// later:
handle.destroy();

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
The host element emits CustomEvents you can listen for:

Event When detail vocadesk:start A call begins — vocadesk:end A call ends { durationMs } vocadesk:error Something went wrong { code, message } 
const el = document.querySelector('[data-vocadesk-embed]');
el.addEventListener('vocadesk:end', (e) => console.log('call length', e.detail.durationMs));
el.addEventListener('vocadesk:error', (e) => console.warn(e.detail.code, e.detail.message));

docs.title: Error codes
docs.text: code Meaning mic_denied The visitor denied microphone access. mic_unavailable No microphone is available. token_failed The call couldn't be authorized (often an origin not on the allowlist). ws_failed The realtime connection couldn't be established. concurrent_call_active This visitor already has a call open for this embed. network A network problem interrupted the call. unknown An unexpected error.

docs.title: Theming
docs.text:
Style the button with CSS custom properties on the host element; size comes from the element's own CSS:

[data-vocadesk-embed] {
  --vocadesk-bg: #1e1b4b;
  --vocadesk-fg: #ffffff;
  --vocadesk-accent: #7c3aed;
  --vocadesk-danger: #ef4444;
  --vocadesk-muted: #a1a1aa;
}

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Origins are enforced. Only domains on the embed's allowed origins can start a call.
  • One call per visitor per embed at a time — see concurrent_call_active.
  • Microphone required. The page must be served over HTTPS and the visitor must grant mic access.
  • No third-party calls. The embed only talks to callcat.ai's own endpoints — no analytics or external trackers — which keeps it safe to add to any site.

docs.title: Web calls & embeds
docs.text: An embed turns a button on your website into a live voice call with an agent — no phone number required. Visitors click, grant microphone access, and talk to the agent right in the browser.

docs.title: Creating an embed
docs.text:
From a client's Embeds tab (or the Embeds area), create an embed and set:

  • Agent — which agent answers these web calls.
  • Allowed origins — the website domains permitted to start calls with this embed (an allowlist). Requests from anywhere else are rejected.
  • Bot protection — optionally require a challenge before a call starts, to deter abuse.

Each embed has an id like emb_abc123.

docs.title: Installing it on a site
docs.text:
Add the embed snippet to the website and place a button that references the embed id. Conceptually:

<!-- Load the Vocadesk embed script (pin a specific version) -->
<script src="https://cdn.vocadesk.com/embed/vX.Y.Z/vocadesk.min.js" defer></script>

<!-- Anywhere you want the call button -->
<button data-vocadesk-embed="emb_abc123">Talk to us</button>

The button handles microphone permission, the call UI, and connecting to the agent. You can also mount it programmatically and style it with CSS variables.

Origins are enforced server-side

Listing your domains under allowed origins isn't just a suggestion — calls from other origins are refused. Add every domain (and subdomain) that should be able to start a call.

docs.title: Web calls in your reports
docs.text: Web calls appear in Calls like any other, with callType: web, full transcripts, recordings, and post-call analysis. Forwarding and conditional instructions work the same as on phone calls — see Conversation design.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: One live call per visitor per embed is allowed at a time, and embeds can have their own concurrency settings. If a visitor already has a call open, starting another is blocked until the first ends.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: This is the shortest path from a new account to an AI agent answering real calls. Each step links to the full detail.

docs.title: 1. Sign in
docs.text: Log in to the dashboard with your email and password, or with your connected identity provider. Your login belongs to an operator — your business workspace — where all your clients, agents, and calls live.

docs.title: 2. Add a client
docs.text: A client is an end-customer whose calls an agent will answer. From Clients → New client, give it a name, industry, and contact details. See Clients.

docs.title: 3. Build an agent
docs.text:
Open the client's Agents tab and create an agent. In a few minutes you can:

  1. Pick a persona and voice.
  2. Write a greeting and a short knowledge base.
  3. Add the intake questions you want from every caller.
  4. Choose a conversation design and, if needed, call-forwarding rules.

docs.title: 4. Test it from your browser
docs.text: Use Test call on the agent page to talk to the agent without touching the phone network. Test calls aren't billed to the client and are marked as test. Iterate on the persona, questions, and forwarding until it sounds right.

docs.title: 5. Go live
docs.text:
• For phone calls: attach a phone number to the agent. Inbound calls to that number are now answered by the agent.
  • For web calls: create an embed and drop its snippet onto your website so visitors can talk to the agent from a button.

docs.title: 6. Review what happened
docs.text:
Every conversation is captured. Open Calls to read transcripts, play recordings, and see the post-call summary, sentiment, and extracted answers.

Do it on a test client first

Spin up a throwaway client and agent to learn the flow before configuring a real one — nothing here is destructive, and test calls are free.

One agent per number

A phone number routes to exactly one agent. To change which agent answers, reassign the number — it can't point at two agents at once.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Quick fixes for the things people hit most often. If something here doesn't resolve it, gather the call (or agent) details and contact support.

docs.title: Agents
docs.text:
The agent answers but I can't hear it on a test call

Test calls run in your browser. Check that your browser tab isn't muted and that audio output is allowed for the page, then place the test call again. The transcript updating while you hear nothing usually points to browser audio, not the agent.

The agent's thumbnail doesn't match its voice

The avatar follows the agent's selected persona. If it ever looks wrong, re-open Change persona and reselect the voice — the picture and the voice are kept in sync.

The agent keeps asking questions instead of transferring

Forwarding only happens on conditions you define, and the condition must be met in full. Make your forwarding conditions specific (what the caller actually says or wants). A vague condition won't reliably trigger.

The agent transfers (or doesn't) at the wrong time

In Questions & conditions, triggers fire on their condition text. Tighten the wording so it matches only the situation you mean.

docs.title: Calls
docs.text:
A call has a transcript but no recording

Recordings are produced after the call. Give it a moment and refresh. Very short or abnormally-ended calls may not have a recording.

I don't see test calls in billing

That's expected — test calls and clients in testing status are never billed. See Billing.

docs.title: Web embeds
docs.text:
The website button does nothing / the call won't start

Confirm the visitor's domain is in the embed's allowed origins. Calls from origins that aren't on the allowlist are refused. Also check that the page can request microphone access.

A visitor can't start a second call

Only one live call per visitor per embed is allowed at a time. End the first call before starting another.

docs.title: Still stuck?
docs.text: Note the client, agent, and (if relevant) the specific call, then reach out to support with those details so it can be traced quickly.

docs.title: Agents
docs.text:
An agent is an AI voice receptionist that belongs to one client. It answers calls in a voice and persona you choose, follows the conversation design you set, collects the information you ask for, and transfers to a human when your rules say so.

Configuring an agent comes down to three decisions:

  • Who it is

    Persona, voice, language, greeting, and the knowledge it can draw on.

    → Configuring an agent

  • How it converses

    Plain intake, conditional instructions, or a full decision tree.

    → Conversation design

  • When it hands off

    Conditions under which the call is transferred to a person.

    → Call forwarding & transfers

docs.title: Creating an agent
docs.text:
1. Open a client and go to its Agents tab.
  2. Select New agent — a persona is suggested based on the client's country.
  3. Adjust the persona, voice, and knowledge.
  4. Choose a conversation design and add your questions.
  5. Add forwarding rules if a human should ever take over.
  6. Test the agent with a browser call before attaching a phone number.

Test before you go live

Use the Test call button on the agent page to talk to the agent from your browser. Nothing is billed to the client and the call is marked as a test.

docs.title: Plan limits
docs.text: How many agents a client can have is set by its subscription plan. When a client is at its limit, the New agent action is disabled with a "plan limit reached" notice — upgrade the client's plan to add more.

docs.title: Advanced agent switches (super-admin)
docs.text: These switches sit in the Advanced (super admin) card of the agent page. Only a super_admin can see or change them. They are per agent, so you can try one on a single agent. The first three are on by default; the last one is off.

docs.title: Reuse confirmed spellings in the email
docs.text:
When the caller's email contains their name or company and they did not spell that part, the agent uses the spelling they already confirmed instead of what it heard. A spelling the caller spells out for the email always wins. This never invents anything: it only reuses a spelling the caller confirmed on the same call.

Turn it off to make the agent use only what it heard for the email.

docs.title: Tuned spelling-accuracy rules
docs.text:
Adds stricter rules so the agent does not blend a spelled name with the version it heard first. Example: it hears "Visaka", the caller spells V-I-S-O-C-K-A, and the agent must store "Visocka", not a mix. It also switches on a small extra check of spelled values by a fast AI model, so each captured spelling costs one small extra model call.

Turn it off to go back to the plain rules for this agent.

docs.title: Dictation mode
docs.text:
When a caller spells an email, name, company, address or postcode, the system itself collects the letters across turns, reads the result back, and takes the yes or no. The AI model no longer decides when a spelling is finished or asks the caller to spell it again.

Turn it off to hand that job back to the model.

docs.title: Runtime asks the next question
docs.text:
After the agent records a caller's answer, the runtime itself says a short "Thanks." and then the agent's next configured question, instead of making a second AI call to write it.

  • Cheaper and faster: one AI call less per answered question, roughly one to two seconds sooner.
  • Fixed wording: the acknowledgement is always the same short phrase.
  • Safe fallback: anything unusual (the caller asks something, changes an earlier answer, interrupts) still goes to the AI as before.
  • Off by default. Super-admin only. Turn it on for one agent, make a test call, and compare how it sounds before using it more widely.

docs.title: Call forwarding & transfers
docs.text:
Call forwarding lets an agent hand a live call to a person when your conditions are met. How you configure it depends on the agent's conversation design:

  • In Questions & forwarding, you use a flat list of forwarding rules.
  • In Questions & conditions, forwarding is a forward action on a trigger.

Both end up doing the same thing at call time.

docs.title: Forwarding rules (simple mode)
docs.text:
Enable Call forwarding on the agent, then add one or more rules. Each rule is:

If <condition in plain language>, transfer to <phone number>.

For example: If the caller has an urgent maintenance issue, transfer to +44 7700 900123.

  • The number must be in international format (with a country code), e.g. +1 555 123 4567.
  • You can add several rules; the agent transfers on the first one whose condition is met in full.

docs.title: Switches for forwarding
docs.text:
• Enable call forwarding is the master switch. While it is off, the agent never transfers, whatever rules you have written. The rules stay saved.
  • Each rule also has its own switch. A rule that is off is skipped, so you can pause one number without deleting the rule.
  • Turn forwarding on only when the numbers are real people who will pick up. A transfer ends the agent's part of the call.

docs.title: Forward triggers (Questions & conditions)
docs.text:
In scenario mode, add a trigger, give it a condition, and enable the Forward action with a number. You can combine say and ask on the same trigger — the agent will say your line and collect any extra questions, then connect the caller.

Forwarding ends the agent's part of the call

When a trigger forwards, the agent does not go back to finish standard intake afterwards. The moment a forward condition applies, the agent connects the caller — it won't keep asking the remaining questions first.

docs.title: How a transfer behaves
docs.text:
When the agent decides to transfer:

  1. It says one short, natural line first — "Sure, let me connect you now, one moment please." — so the caller always hears the hand-off.
  2. It connects the caller in the same turn (it never promises a transfer and then forgets to do it, and it never announces the transfer twice).
  3. A transfer is not treated as the end of the call — the agent doesn't say goodbye or sign off; it just connects.

docs.title: Caller asks for a human, but no condition matches
docs.text:
If a caller simply asks to speak to someone without meeting a specific forwarding condition, the agent does not transfer. Instead it explains that it's the AI assistant handling the line, assures the caller their details will reach the right person, and continues collecting information.

Make conditions explicit

Transfers only happen on conditions you define. If you want "asks for a manager" to forward, add that as an explicit condition.

docs.title: Channel differences
docs.text:
• Phone (PSTN) calls are transferred by dialing the configured number.
  • Web and test calls signal the browser to hand off — no outbound phone call is placed from the server.

docs.title: Verifying it works
docs.text: Place a test call and trigger your condition out loud. You should hear the agent's connecting line, after which the transfer is signalled. Test calls won't dial a real phone, so this confirms the decision, not the dialing.

docs.title: Catalog & order taking
docs.text: An agent can know your products and take orders on the call. This card appears on the agent page only when a super-admin has turned on Order taking for your operator.

docs.title: Catalog / product info
docs.text:
Turn this on and the agent answers questions about your items, prices and what is available, using the menu you build below the switch. It works without order taking, so you can use it as a product guide only.

When the switch is off the agent does not know the menu, and order taking is switched off too (it needs the catalog).

docs.title: Order taking
docs.text:
Turn this on (the catalog must be on first) and the agent takes an order during the call: it checks each item against the menu, asks for sizes and add-ons, and records the order. Every finished order is emailed to the Order notification email you set in the menu editor.

If order taking is not available on the platform at that moment, the agent simply carries on without it; the call does not fail.

Cost

The menu is added to what the agent reads, so a very large menu makes each call a little heavier. The editor warns you when a catalog is large.

docs.title: Show prices to callers
docs.text: On by default. Turn it off to keep prices out of the call completely: the agent will not quote or discuss them, even if asked, and says pricing is not available over the phone. You can still keep prices in the menu for your own records.

docs.title: Ask quantity for every item
docs.text: When on, the agent always asks how many before adding an item. When off, it assumes one unless the caller says a number. Turn it on for items people usually order in numbers (tickets, pastries).

docs.title: Item available
docs.text: Each item has an Available switch. An item that is off is left out of what the agent knows, so it will not offer it or take it in an order. The item stays in your catalog; switch it back on when it is in stock again.

docs.title: Add-on group: Required
docs.text: An add-on group (toppings, sauces, sizes of side) is either Pick one or Pick any. Tick Required and the agent must get a choice from that group before the item is added: one choice for "Pick one", at least one for "Pick any". Leave it unticked and the add-on is optional.

docs.title: Configuring an agent
docs.text: This page covers who the agent is — its persona, voice, and what it knows and asks. For how it runs the conversation, see Conversation design; for hand-off, see Call forwarding.

docs.title: Persona
docs.text:
A persona is a ready-made package of voice + personality + language, shown with a photo and a short description (for example "Warm and professional British receptionist"). Choosing a persona sets a sensible default voice, greeting, and language in one click.

  • Open Change persona on the agent page to browse personas.
  • Personas are grouped by language — pick the language first, then the voice.
  • The persona's avatar follows the agent everywhere it appears (the agents list, the edit page), so the picture always matches the selected voice.

Some personas are restricted

A few personas (for example Hebrew-language voices) are only available to super-admin users.

docs.title: Voice & language
docs.text: Each persona maps to a specific voice from a speech provider. The agent speaks — and expects to hear — the persona's language. If a caller switches language mid-call, the agent keeps replying in its configured language unless told otherwise.

docs.title: Greeting & opening question
docs.text:
The greeting is the first thing the agent says when it picks up, for example:

"Thank you for calling Elegant Homes, this is Grace. How can I help you today?"

A good greeting names the business, names the agent, and invites the caller to explain why they're calling. The caller's answer is scanned immediately for anything that already answers one of your intake questions, so the agent never re-asks for something the caller just told it.

docs.title: Knowledge base
docs.text:
The knowledge base is free-text the agent can use to answer factual questions about the business — hours, services, pricing, location, process. If a caller asks something covered here, the agent answers first, then continues collecting any information it still needs.

Answer first, collect second

Callers' questions take priority. The agent will answer from the knowledge base before pushing on with intake — this feels natural and avoids interrogations.

docs.title: Intake questions
docs.text:
Intake questions are the structured information you want from every caller — name, phone number, reason for calling, and so on. Each question has:

  • the spoken question the agent asks,
  • an internal field name used to store the answer (never read aloud), and
  • a type (text, phone, email, …) and whether it's required.

The agent asks one question at a time, skips anything the caller already provided, and validates answers as they're given (for example, reading an email address back phonetically to confirm spelling).

Reorder questions by dragging them; the order is the order they're asked.

docs.title: Switching a question off
docs.text: Each question has an on/off switch. A question that is off stays in your list but the agent does not ask it, so you can pause a question and bring it back later without retyping it. Questions are on by default.

docs.title: Auto-fix English words written in Hebrew
docs.text:
This switch shows only on agents whose language is Hebrew. It is on by default.

People often type English names and terms in Hebrew letters, for example "וורקאאוט" for "workout". The voice would then read them the Hebrew way. With the switch on, each time you save, the system rewrites those words into proper English in your greeting, persona, knowledge base and questions. The result is what the agent says on the call.

  • Turn it off if you want the text kept exactly as you typed it.
  • It runs when you save, not during a call, so it does not slow a call down.
  • It only changes words that are phonetic English; normal Hebrew is left alone.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text: Changes autosave as you edit. A status indicator shows "All changes saved" once a change has persisted.

docs.text:
Conversation design is how an agent runs the call. callcat.ai offers three modes, from simplest to most powerful. You pick one per agent on the agent page.

Mode Best for Who can use it Questions & forwarding Straight intake plus simple "if X, transfer" rules. Existing agents already using it (legacy). Questions & conditions Intake plus instructions that fire only when a topic comes up. Everyone — the default for new agents. Decision tree Fully scripted, branching conversations. Operators a super admin has enabled it for.

Defaults and availability

New agents start in Questions & conditions. Questions & forwarding is a legacy mode kept only for agents that already use it, so their setup is preserved. Decision tree is off by default; a super admin enables it per operator (Super Admin dashboard → Operators → Decision tree toggle), and it then appears in the mode switcher for every agent under that operator.

docs.title: Questions & forwarding (simple)
docs.text:
The classic setup: the agent works through your intake questions and, separately, applies a flat list of call-forwarding rules — "if the caller says X, transfer to this number."

Use it when intake and forwarding are independent and you don't need the agent to change its behavior based on what the caller says.

docs.title: Questions & conditions (scenario)
docs.text:
The recommended mode. You keep your standard intake questions and add conditional instructions — called triggers — that only activate when a condition is met.

A trigger has:

  • a condition in plain language (for example "the caller wants to book a viewing"), and
  • one or more actions: say something, ask extra questions, and/or forward the call.

When a caller raises a topic that matches a trigger, the agent acts on it immediately — even mid-intake — instead of finishing every standard question first.

Write specific conditions

Vague conditions ("the caller needs help") make the agent fire triggers at the wrong time, or miss them. Be concrete about what the caller says or wants.

docs.title: Turning a trigger off
docs.text:
Each trigger has an on/off switch. A trigger that is off is ignored on calls and its details are folded away, but it stays in your list. Use it to pause a rule (for example a seasonal offer) without losing the wording.

Forwarding is just an action on a trigger here — see Call forwarding & transfers for how that behaves.

docs.title: Decision tree (advanced)
docs.text:
A decision tree scripts the whole call as a branching flow: each step is either a yes/no condition or an action (say something, collect a field, transfer, answer from knowledge, or end). It replaces standard intake entirely and gives you precise control over every branch.

Decision tree suits complex, highly-regulated, or heavily-scripted call flows. A super admin must enable it for your operator before it appears in the mode switcher below.

docs.title: Required steps
docs.text: A collect step has a Required box. When it is ticked, the agent must get that answer before it moves on. If the caller hesitates or declines, the agent explains why it is needed and asks again, patiently. You can write that explanation in the insist box; if you leave it empty the agent makes a short one up. Only if the caller firmly refuses after several tries does the agent give up on that step. When the box is not ticked, the agent tries about twice, then moves on if the caller can't or won't answer.

docs.title: Switching modes
docs.text: The mode switcher on the agent page only shows the modes available to you. Switching to Questions & conditions brings your existing forwarding rules across as forward-only triggers, so nothing is lost.

docs.title: Testing your agent
docs.text: Before attaching a phone number or publishing a web button, talk to your agent from the browser. Test calls let you hear exactly how it sounds and behaves, and iterate fast — at no cost.

docs.title: Placing a test call
docs.text:
Open the agent and use Test call. Your browser asks for microphone access, then you're connected straight to the agent. Talk to it as a caller would.

  • Test calls are not billed to the client and are recorded with callType: test.
  • They appear in Calls like any other call, with a transcript and recording, so you can review what happened afterwards.

Use a testing client

Keep a client in testing status for experiments — its calls are never billed, so you can iterate freely.

docs.title: Test-call modes
docs.text:
The dashboard can place a test call a few different ways. They all talk to the same agent; pick whichever connects cleanly for you:

Mode What it is Native A direct in-browser call to the voice runtime — the default, lowest-overhead path. Phone (Twilio) Routes the browser call through the telephone stack, closer to a real inbound call. Comparison A vendor agent mode, for comparing behavior side by side.

docs.title: What to check before going live
docs.text:
• Greeting — does it name your business and the agent, and invite the caller in?
  • Knowledge — ask the factual questions a caller would; confirm the agent answers from its knowledge base before pushing on with intake.
  • Intake — give partial information up front and confirm the agent skips questions you've already answered and asks for what's missing.
  • Forwarding — trigger each forwarding condition out loud and confirm the agent connects (on a test call the transfer is signalled — no real number is dialled, so you're verifying the decision, not the dialing).
  • Voice & language — the right voice and language for your audience.

docs.title: Going live
docs.text:
When it sounds right:

  • For phone: attach a phone number.
  • For web: publish an embed button.

Then review real conversations in Calls and keep tuning.

docs.title: Voices & languages
docs.text: An agent's voice and language come from its persona. Picking a persona sets a natural-sounding voice and the language the agent speaks and understands — but you can preview and compare options before committing.

docs.title: Choosing a voice
docs.text:
In the persona picker, choose a language first, then a voice within it. Each voice has a short description (warm, professional, upbeat, calm, …) and a photo that becomes the agent's avatar.

  • Preview before you pick — play the sample on each persona to hear it.
  • The avatar and voice stay in sync, so the picture in your agents list always matches how the agent sounds.

docs.title: Comparing voices
docs.text: The Voice audio manager lets you listen to the available voices side by side, so you can settle on the right tone for your audience before configuring an agent.

docs.title: Language behavior
docs.text:
The agent conducts the whole call in its configured language — greeting, questions, and replies. If a caller switches language mid-call, the agent keeps responding in its language unless you've designed it to do otherwise.

Pick the language that matches the people who'll call. The persona's language also shapes the accent, so an English (UK) persona sounds different from English (US).

Some voices and languages are restricted

A few voices and languages (for example native Hebrew voices) are only available to super-admin users. See Administration.

docs.title: Appointment bookings (Cliniko)
docs.text:
With bookings, an agent can look up a caller's upcoming appointment in Cliniko, move it to another time or cancel it, all during the call. The caller is identified first, the agent reads the change back, and nothing is written to Cliniko until the caller says yes.

This page is the reference for the Bookings tab. The Cliniko user manual walks through the whole feature:

Page What it covers Set up Cliniko bookings Preparing Cliniko, connecting it, choosing settings, switching agents on, testing and going live What happens on a booking call What the caller is asked and hears, step by step, and when the agent takes a message instead Running bookings day to day Audit log, alert emails, summary emails, the patient email, nightly checks, data deletion, changing or removing the key Bookings troubleshooting Common problems and questions, and how to fix them

docs.title: Who sees the Bookings tab
docs.text:
Bookings live on the Bookings tab of a client, between Embeds and Info. The tab is for operator admins and super-admins; regular users don't see it.

  • Operator admins see the tab only once a super-admin has switched Bookings on for their operator (see Administration).
  • Super-admins always see it. While the operator's switch is off they get a banner, and connecting, saving settings and switching agents on are refused. Only Disconnect still works.

docs.title: What v1 does and does not do
docs.text:
• It moves and cancels existing appointments. It does not create new bookings or patients, and it never writes to a patient's record.
  • It works for scenario-mode, English agents only.
  • A move keeps the same practitioner and appointment type. Anything else becomes a message for the clinic.

docs.title: Connect Cliniko
docs.text:
Create a dedicated Cliniko user with the minimum role that can view patients and manage appointments, generate the API key from that user, and paste it into the Cliniko connection card. A key carries the full permissions of the user who made it, so a narrow role limits the damage if the key ever leaks. Set up Cliniko bookings has the step-by-step version.

After you connect, the card shows:

  • the last 4 characters of the key, never the key itself (it is stored encrypted and can't be read back);
  • the key owner and their role, with a warning if the role is broad (Administrator, Bookkeeper or Power receptionist);
  • the status (Connected, Key rejected or Disconnected), when the key was last verified, and the last error if there was one.

The key is re-verified every night. Use Re-verify to check it now.

Role too narrow

If Cliniko refuses one of the requests the connection needs, the card says This Cliniko user's role is too narrow. Give that user a role that can view patients and manage appointments, or generate the key from a different user, then re-verify or replace the key.

Replace key swaps in a new key. The new key is checked first, and your settings and agents are kept. An agent whose businesses are no longer valid for the new key loses its bookings switch. If Cliniko rejects a key at any time, the connection is marked Key rejected and bookings are switched off for all of the client's agents until you replace it.

docs.title: Disconnecting
docs.text: Disconnect deletes our stored copy of the key immediately and switches bookings off for all of the client's agents. Settings are not kept: connecting again starts from the defaults. The key stays valid in Cliniko until you archive it there, so archive it in Cliniko too. The panel reminds you after you disconnect.

docs.title: Businesses and what can be changed by phone
docs.text:
This card lists the Cliniko businesses the key can see. Each shows whether it is Online-bookable, its timezone, and the practitioner and appointment type combinations that are enabled for online booking, with their length.

Phone offers follow your Cliniko online-booking limits. An appointment can be moved by phone only when its business, practitioner and appointment type are all enabled for online booking and it is no longer than the appointment type's length. Any other appointment can be cancelled by phone but not moved. Moving it becomes a message for the clinic.

The card also shows About N booking flows per minute at once: an estimate of what the connection's Cliniko rate limit allows (about 10 for one Cliniko user). It is not a guarantee, and the limit is shared with any other software using the same Cliniko user.

If online booking is switched off in Cliniko altogether, no appointment can be moved by phone. Cancelling is still possible. A business whose timezone can't be worked out is marked Timezone unknown and bookings are blocked there. Notes from the last check lists anything else Cliniko's answer raised.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Each setting has its own ? button. Save is enabled once something has changed and saves only what you changed.

docs.title: How callers are verified
docs.text:
What the agent asks for before it reads out any appointment. Options: Date of birth (the default), Full name, Surname and date of birth, or Full name and date of birth. The caller ID is also matched against the phone numbers Cliniko holds for the patient.

Caller ID can be spoofed

Caller ID is not authenticated. With the default (date of birth only), someone who calls from a spoofed number and knows a patient's date of birth can reach that patient's appointments. A stricter set of details lowers the risk. Record this limit in your data protection impact assessment.

docs.title: Callers with no caller ID
docs.text:
Withheld numbers, the web widget and the browser test call have no number to match. The agent asks for these details instead: Surname and date of birth (the default), Full name and date of birth, or Don't book: take a message.

Weaker than a number on file

Without a caller ID the details alone open the record, which is weaker than calling from a number held in Cliniko. The web widget and the browser test call need no login. Repeated wrong guesses are limited by the daily cap.

docs.title: Details match, but the number isn't on file
docs.text:
What happens when the caller's details match one patient whose phone numbers don't include the number they're calling from: Take a message (the default), or Ask for the full name too, and accept.

The full-name option tells callers their details matched

With the full-name option the agent asks for more details only in this case, so callers learn that their details matched a patient. With Take a message the caller hears the same thing whether the details or the number was wrong.

docs.title: After a change
docs.text: What the agent does once an appointment has been moved or cancelled: Carry on with the intake questions (the default), or Close with a booking line: the agent confirms the change ("Your appointment is now Friday the 15th of November at 10am with Dana."), asks whether there is anything else, and skips the intake questions.

docs.title: Email to the patient
docs.text: Optionally send the patient an email after a change: No email (the default) or Send an email. It goes to the address Cliniko holds for the patient, never to the calling number. Each email is its own cost line in your price. Cliniko can already email patients about changes, so check that patients don't get two. Running bookings day to day shows what the email says.

docs.title: Cancellation notice
docs.text:
Applies to cancelling and to rescheduling. Inside the window the agent takes a message instead of making the change. Options: Use Cliniko's rule (its minimum notice for patient cancellations), Custom hours (whole hours, 1 to 8760), or No notice window.

The panel shows Cliniko's current value. If Cliniko's notice is unset or 0, you must choose Custom hours, and agents can't have bookings switched on until you do.

docs.title: Keep call data for
docs.text:
Transcripts, recordings, summaries and extracted data of this client's booking-agent calls are deleted after this many days (default 90, range 1 to 3650). The change applies to this client only. Running bookings day to day lists exactly which calls are covered.

Recordings hold the date of birth

Dates of birth are removed from transcripts, but a recording still holds the spoken date of birth until it is deleted under this rule. Confirm the number against your agreement with the clinic.

docs.title: No-caller-ID daily cap
docs.text: The number of failed verifications allowed per day on calls without a caller ID (default 10, range 0 to 1000). When it is reached, bookings on such calls stop for this client until the next day (UTC). Set it to 0 to stop them straight away.

docs.title: Switch bookings on for an agent
docs.text:
The Agents card appears once Cliniko is connected. Each agent has a bookings switch and a Businesses picker. Tick the Cliniko business or businesses the agent may act for, then turn the switch on. To change the businesses of an agent that is already on, change the ticks and press Save businesses.

The switch can only be turned on while the connection is Connected and the operator's Bookings switch is on. It is greyed out, with a note, for an agent that is disabled, not in scenario mode, or not English. A business that isn't online-bookable can't be ticked.

If the switch is refused, the reason shows under the agent. The rules are:

  • Cliniko is connected and verified;
  • at least one business is chosen, every chosen business is online-bookable, and the chosen businesses share one timezone;
  • Cliniko's cancellation notice is set (or you've set custom hours).

Switching an agent off is always allowed. Turning an agent's switch off, or disconnecting Cliniko, takes effect during a live call: the agent takes a message at the next booking step. Duplicating an agent to a different client does not copy its bookings settings.

docs.title: Audit log
docs.text:
Every read and change an agent makes in Cliniko is logged, newest first, 50 rows at a time (Load older for more). Columns: Time, Action, Outcome, Agent, Call (a View call link), Details and Time taken.

Actions: Looked up patient, Verification failed, Listed appointments, Looked up free times, Rescheduled, Moved back, Cancelled and Checked the connection. Use it to review the first calls of a new agent. Running bookings day to day explains the outcomes.

The log never stores patient names, dates of birth or phone numbers.

docs.title: What happens on a booking call
docs.text: This page follows a booking call from the caller's side. The quoted lines are the fixed words the agent says. Other wording comes from the agent's conversation and varies from call to call. The examples use an appointment with Dana on Tuesday the 12th of November at 2:30pm.

docs.title: When the booking steps start
docs.text:
At any point in the call, a caller who wants to look up, check, change, move, reschedule or cancel an appointment they already have is taken into the booking steps. The agent recognises this from what the caller says; there is no keyword to say. It comes before the agent's other triggers about appointments.

The booking steps aren't offered:

  • on an agent without the bookings switch, or one that isn't in scenario mode;
  • while the agent is forwarding the call or ending it.

A caller who wants a new appointment, a different practitioner or a different appointment type gets a message taken for the clinic: v1 only moves and cancels existing appointments.

docs.title: 1. Verifying the caller
docs.text:
The agent asks for the details set in How callers are verified, one at a time:

Setting The caller is asked for Date of birth (default) date of birth Full name full name Surname and date of birth surname, then date of birth Full name and date of birth full name, then date of birth

If the call has no caller ID (withheld number, web widget, browser test call), the details from Callers with no caller ID are added, surname and date of birth by default. If that setting is Don't book: take a message, the agent says "I can't confirm that on this call, so I'll take a message for the clinic." straight away.

  • Names are captured the same careful way as names in the intake questions, with spelling and a read-back.
  • The date of birth is read back in words, for example "The fourth of March nineteen eighty-five, is that right?". The lookup only runs after a clear yes. A future date, or one more than 120 years ago, is asked for again.
  • The agent says "One moment while I check." while it looks the patient up.

How the match works. The details must match a Cliniko patient exactly, ignoring capitals, accents, hyphens, apostrophes and spaces (José Smith-Jones matches jose smithjones). There is no guessing at near matches. A full name may use the patient's first name or their preferred first name. When there is a caller ID, it must be one of the phone numbers Cliniko holds for that patient. If it isn't, the unknown-number setting decides: take a message (default), or ask for the full name too.

If the details don't match, the caller hears that no booking was found with those details, without being told which detail was wrong, and is asked once more for all of them. After a second failure the agent says "I can't confirm that on this call, so I'll take a message for the clinic." and returns to the rest of the call. The booking steps aren't offered again on that call.

Other limits stop repeated guessing across calls. When one is reached, the caller hears the same "take a message" line:

Limit Value Failed verifications per call 2 Failed verifications per calling number, per day 6 Failed number checks against one patient, per day 6 (that patient can't be verified by phone for the rest of the day) Failed verifications on calls with no caller ID, per client, per day the daily cap, 10 by default

Days are counted in UTC. If two patients fit the same details equally well (for example twins calling from a shared number), the agent can't tell them apart and takes a message.

Once verified, the caller stays verified for the rest of the call. A call can only act on one patient's appointments.

docs.title: 2. Finding the appointment
docs.text:
The agent reads out up to three upcoming appointments, nearest first, with the practitioner and the time, for example "Tuesday the 12th of November at 2:30pm with Dana". If there are several, the caller can pick by order ("the second one"), day ("the Tuesday one") or practitioner. Only appointments at the businesses chosen for the agent are listed.

  • No upcoming appointment: the agent says it can't find a booking under those details, and offers to take a message, or to transfer the call if the agent has forwarding set up.
  • An appointment that can't be moved by phone (not online-bookable, or longer than its appointment type): the agent offers to cancel it or take a message.
  • An appointment inside the cancellation notice window: it can't be moved or cancelled by phone. The agent takes a message.

When the agent takes a message it says "I'll pass that on to the clinic." and carries on with the call; the message is in the call's summary.

docs.title: 3a. Moving an appointment
docs.text:
1. The agent looks up free times for the same practitioner and appointment type at the same business, up to four weeks ahead and within the clinic's online-booking lead time and booking window ("One moment while I check.").
  2. It offers three times at a time, in the clinic's local time. The caller can ask for a day, a date range, or the morning (before 12), afternoon (12 to 5pm) or evening (after 5pm). "Anything later?" gives the next three.
  3. If nothing is free in that range, the agent offers a later window once, then takes a message.
  4. When the caller picks a time, the agent reads the change back: "I'll move your appointment with Dana from Tuesday the 12th of November at 2:30pm to Friday the 15th of November at 10am. Shall I go ahead?"
  5. Only a clear yes makes the change ("yes", "yeah", "go ahead", "that's right", "yes, Friday at 10 is fine"). "Yes, but make it 3", "wait", "I guess so" or a yes followed by "actually…" are not a yes. If the answer is unclear, the agent asks "Shall I go ahead and move it to Friday at 10am?", then "Shall I leave it as it is?". Anything but a clear go-ahead leaves the appointment alone: "No problem, I'll leave your appointment as it is."
  6. After the yes: "One moment while I make that change.", then "Your appointment is now Friday the 15th of November at 10am with Dana."

If the time was taken meanwhile, the agent says so, looks again once and offers new times. If someone else booked the same time in the moment the change was made, the move is undone: "I'm sorry, that time was just taken by someone else, so your appointment stays as it was, Tuesday the 12th of November at 2:30pm with Dana." The clinic gets an alert email.

In Cliniko the appointment simply moves, keeping its length. No note is added.

docs.title: 3b. Cancelling an appointment
docs.text:
1. The agent reads it back: "I'll cancel your appointment with Dana on Tuesday the 12th of November at 2:30pm. Shall I go ahead?"
  2. Only a clear yes cancels it ("yes, cancel it"). Unclear answers get "Shall I go ahead and cancel it?", then "Shall I leave it as it is?".
  3. After the yes: "Your appointment on Tuesday the 12th of November at 2:30pm is cancelled."

In Cliniko the appointment is cancelled with a cancellation reason the agent picks from what the caller said (feeling better, condition worse, sick, away, work or other) and the note "Cancelled by phone agent at caller's request". Repeats of the appointment are not cancelled.

docs.title: 4. After the change
docs.text:
What happens next follows After a change:

  • Carry on with the intake questions (default): the agent goes on with the agent's next unanswered question.
  • Close with a booking line: the agent asks whether there is anything else, and if not, ends the call with the booking line before the goodbye.

If the caller changes their mind after a change, the agent takes a message for the clinic; it doesn't undo the change itself. If Email to the patient is on, the patient gets an email about the change.

docs.title: When something goes wrong
docs.text:
Situation The caller hears Cliniko is down, slow or busy, or the key stopped working "Sorry, I can't do that right now. I'll pass that on to the clinic." The change was sent but Cliniko didn't confirm it in time "I couldn't confirm that went through; the clinic will confirm with you." The clinic gets an alert email to check the appointment. Bookings were switched off for the agent or operator, or Cliniko was disconnected, during the call A "take a message" line at the next booking step.

The agent never retries a change on its own, so a change can't be made twice.

docs.title: What the call record shows
docs.text:
• Transcript: every date of birth is replaced with [date of birth], in the caller's and the agent's turns. Appointment times stay.
  • Recording: still holds the spoken date of birth until it is deleted under Keep call data for.
  • Summary and extracted data: never include a date of birth or appointment type. Only the agent's own question fields are kept in the extracted data.
  • Summary email: an Appointment section with one line per outcome. See Running bookings day to day.
  • Audit log: one row per lookup and change. See Running bookings day to day.

docs.title: Running bookings day to day
docs.text: Once a clinic is live, most of the work is reading: the audit log, the call summaries and the occasional alert email. This page explains each, plus the jobs that run on their own and how to change or remove the Cliniko key.

docs.title: The first week
docs.text:
For a new agent, check these every day for the first week:

  • the Audit log on the Bookings tab: lots of Verification failed rows can mean patients' phone numbers or dates of birth are missing in Cliniko, or that the verification setting is too strict for the clinic's patients;
  • the booking calls themselves in Calls: listen to a few, and check the changes in Cliniko;
  • any alert email.

docs.title: The audit log
docs.text:
The Audit log card lists every read and change agents made in Cliniko, newest first, with a View call link for each row. It is append-only and never stores patient names, dates of birth, phone numbers or the key.

Action Meaning Looked up patient The agent searched for the caller. Details shows how many patients matched. Verification failed The caller's details or number didn't match. Listed appointments The agent read the patient's upcoming appointments. Looked up free times The agent searched for times to offer. Rescheduled An appointment was moved. Moved back A move was undone because another patient took the time. Cancelled An appointment was cancelled. Checked the connection The key was checked: at connect, on Re-verify, on Replace key or overnight.

The Outcome is OK when the step worked. Other outcomes:

Outcome Meaning Refused The caller wasn't verified or a verification limit was reached (also when Cliniko refused a request). Not allowed The change isn't allowed by phone, for example inside the cancellation notice window. Not found No matching patient or appointment. Not supported / Not bookable online The appointment can't be moved by phone. No free times No time was free in the range the caller asked about. Time was taken The chosen time went before the change was made. Unconfirmed The change was sent but couldn't be confirmed. Check it in Cliniko. Key rejected Cliniko refused the key. Role too narrow Cliniko refused a request because of the key owner's role. Unavailable / Rate limited Cliniko was down, slow or busy.

docs.title: Alert emails
docs.text:
Some events email the clinic straight away. Alerts go to the addresses in Call Summary Recipients on the client's Info tab, or to its Contact Email if that list is empty, and include the call ID.

Subject What happened What to do A booking change could not be confirmed A change was sent to Cliniko but couldn't be confirmed. The caller was told the clinic will confirm. Check the appointment in Cliniko and call the patient back. A booking change was undone A move was undone because another patient took the time at the same moment. The appointment is back where it was. Usually nothing. Call the patient back if they still need a new time. A moved appointment overlaps another booking A move went through but overlaps another entry in the practitioner's diary. Check the diary and fix the overlap. Your practice system connection stopped working Cliniko rejected the key. Bookings are off for all of the client's agents. Replace the key.

docs.title: The summary email
docs.text:
On a booking call, the call-summary email has an Appointment section with one line per outcome, for example:

  • "Appointment moved from Tuesday 12 November at 2:30 pm to Friday 15 November at 10:00 am."
  • "Appointment on Tuesday 12 November at 2:30 pm cancelled (sick)."
  • "Move attempted and undone because the new time was taken. The appointment stays on …"
  • "Could not confirm that the reschedule went through. Please check the appointment in your practice system."
  • "The caller could not be verified; a message was taken."
  • "The caller decided to keep their appointment."
  • "No matching appointment was found."
  • "No free times were found; a message was taken."
  • "The appointment can only be moved by the clinic; a message was taken."

If the caller changed their mind after a change, the line ends with "The caller changed their mind afterwards; a message was taken."

docs.title: The email to the patient
docs.text:
With Email to the patient set to Send an email, the patient gets an email after a move or cancel that stands. It is not sent for a move that was undone, or if Cliniko holds no email address for the patient.

  • From: the operator's summary-email sender, or no-reply@callcat.ai.
  • Subject: "Your appointment has been moved - clinic name" or "Your appointment has been cancelled - clinic name".
  • Body: "Your appointment with Dana has been moved from Tuesday 12 November at 2:30 pm to Friday 15 November at 10:00 am." (or "…on time has been cancelled."), then "This was arranged by phone. If this is not right, please contact clinic name."

Each email is a Patient notice email cost line on the call.

docs.title: Jobs that run on their own
docs.text:
• Overnight key check. Every connected key is checked once a night. Businesses, practitioners, appointment types and Cliniko's notice are refreshed, and an agent whose businesses are no longer online-bookable loses its bookings switch. If Cliniko rejects the key, the connection becomes Key rejected, bookings are switched off for all the client's agents and the clinic gets an alert. A rejected key isn't checked again until you replace it.
  • Daily data deletion. See below.

After changing something in Cliniko (a new practitioner, an appointment type shown online, a new notice), press Re-verify to pick it up straight away.

docs.title: Data deletion
docs.text:
Every day, call data older than Keep call data for (90 days by default) is deleted for these calls of the client:

  • calls with a booking outcome or an audit-log row;
  • every call of an agent that currently has bookings on, including calls from before bookings were switched on.

The transcript, summary, extracted data and recording are deleted. The call itself stays in the calls list with its booking outcome, so billing and counts are unaffected. This still runs after Cliniko is disconnected.

docs.title: Change the key
docs.text:
Replace the key when it is rejected, when the Cliniko user leaves, or as a routine change.

  1. Create a new key in Cliniko (see Set up Cliniko bookings).
  2. On the Bookings tab, press Replace key, paste the new key and press Replace. The new key is checked first; settings and agents are kept.
  3. If the connection was Key rejected, turn the agents' switches back on. A rejected key switches them all off.
  4. Archive the old key in Cliniko.

docs.title: Stop bookings
docs.text:
To stop… Do this What's kept One agent Turn its switch off in the Agents card. Everything else. One clinic Disconnect on the connection card, then archive the key in Cliniko. Nothing: the key and settings are deleted; agents' switches go off. A whole operator A super-admin turns the operator's Bookings switch off (see Administration). Everything, ready to turn back on.

Each takes effect straight away, even on a call in progress.
